title: Coarse-Grained Model for Mechanosensitive Ion Channels
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B

l3_target.description: a plant ion channel that opens when the membrane is stretched
l3_target.shared_feature: tension-dependent gating of a mechanosensitive channel

evidence.caveat: MSL10 may differ substantially from bacterial MscS in oligomeric organization, transmembrane topology, cytoplasmic domains, lipid interactions, and gating mechanism; the seed model and parameters would therefore require substantial reparameterization and validation rather than direct reuse.

title: Key Intermolecular Interactions in the E. coli 70S Ribosome Revealed by Coarse-Grained Analysis
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

l3_target.description: the plastid ribosome, a two-subunit bacterial-type ribosome with plastid-specific additions
l3_target.shared_feature: inter-subunit contacts and collective motions of a two-subunit ribosome

evidence.caveat: E. coli-derived interaction strengths and domain definitions should not be transferred unchanged: chloroplast ribosomes contain lineage-specific RNAs and proteins, and a chloroplast-specific all-atom reference structure or experimental data would be needed for calibration and validation.

title: Monitoring the binding and insertion of a single transmembrane protein by an insertase

l3_target.description: a thylakoid-membrane insertase that inserts transmembrane proteins into the membrane
l3_target.shared_feature: binding and insertion of a single transmembrane protein by an insertase

evidence.caveat: Alb3 may differ from bacterial YidC in domain architecture, topology, stromal targeting context, membrane composition, and substrate specificity; therefore the detailed role of the YidC cytoplasmic hairpin and the reported millisecond kinetics may not transfer directly.

title: Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics Simulations of a Rotating Bacterial Flagellum

l3_target.description: the rotating helical motility filament of archaea
l3_target.shared_feature: rotation and torque transmission of a long helical protein filament

evidence.caveat: Bacterial flagellar filaments and archaella are not homologous and differ substantially in subunit architecture, filament mechanics, motor coupling, and torque generation; the seed force field and structural model would therefore require substantial reparameterization, and its treatment of motor-driven torque may not directly transfer.

title: Modeling DNA Opening in the Eukaryotic Transcription Initiation Complexes via Coarse-Grained Models
named_system: RNA polymerase II transcription initiation complex

l3_target.description: the archaeal RNA polymerase, which initiates transcription with TBP- and TFB-type factors
l3_target.shared_feature: promoter DNA opening during transcription initiation
l3_target.source_system: RNA polymerase II transcription initiation complex

evidence.caveat: The yeast Pol II initiation complex includes eukaryote-specific factors and structural elements, while Sulfolobus promoter recognition, initiation factors, RNAP subunits, and DNA sequences differ; the reported fork-loop mechanism and any CG interaction parameters therefore cannot be transferred directly without archaeal structural data and reparameterization.

title: Membrane Constriction by Dynamin through GTP-Driven Conformational Changes from Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics Simulations
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters

l3_target.description: a yeast mitochondrial GTPase that assembles on the inner membrane and remodels it
l3_target.shared_feature: nucleotide-dependent assembly that constricts a membrane

evidence.caveat: Mgm1 may differ substantially from dynamin in oligomeric architecture, membrane topology, mitochondrial localization, and the molecular mechanism of remodeling; the seed's specific dynamin conformational changes and ring behavior cannot be assumed to apply directly.
